question: How sensitive is the accepted finite-window attractor-density reconstruction to sampling, temporal dependence, histogram resolution and smoothing?
hypotheses: Denser sampling of the same fixed trajectory window can separate temporal quadrature error from between-law variation
Independent random time-index reconstruction estimates sampling variability conditional on a fixed path
Histogram and smoothing choices may change full densities materially despite stable statistics
Serial dependence and block-length choices can invalidate independent-sample uncertainty interpretations
metrics: observable-specific autocorrelation, truncated correlation time and heuristic ESS
sensitivity versus count, phase, histogram and physical smoothing width

thresholds.technical_completion: Every frozen law/comparison and required metadata recorded; hashes/provenance/seal complete
thresholds.scientific_qualification: NOT_AUTHORIZED_BY_CHARACTERIZATION: gate stays OPEN pending owner-reviewed reconstruction recipe and scientifically justified error budget, followed by a new predeclared qualification run

required_evidence: bitwise replay of all six historical trajectory windows
new dense path hashes and reference densities
conditional independent reconstruction and block-length diagnostics
histogram comparison at fixed physical bandwidth
config, commit, input/output hashes, actual command/runtime and final seal
pass_consequences: Technical characterization completion provides evidence only; G02 remains OPEN and G03 LOCKED. Propose justified recipe/error budget and a new qualification study.
failure_consequences: Preserve failed run and diagnostics; G02 remains OPEN or FAILED on adjudication. No threshold relaxation, data replacement or training.
review_requirements: Owner approval of a scientific reconstruction-error budget is required before gate qualification
Do not promote low-dimensional statistics or heuristic ESS into density accuracy
Preserve inspected source laws as development evidence
limitations: Fixed ten-unit windows are not stationary occupation-law certification
Dense RK4 replay at the same integration dt does not establish continuum ODE accuracy
IID time-index draws are conditional on one fixed discrete path; different trajectories belong to G03
Block resampling and ESS are dependence diagnostics, not confidence/coverage guarantees
Different smoothing widths define different regularized laws
Histogram comparisons retain grid-dependent vertex lifting
Learning-grid diagnostics do not certify G05 resolution adequacy
Six inspected historical laws are development evidence; qualification requires fresh predeclared evidence
